questions.question: In an ecosystem why is the number of trophic levels of a food chain usually limited?

options.text: Lower trophic level has lesser energy than the higher trophic level
Because of the loss of energy at each trophic level
Higher trophic level individual can control the lower ones more
Limited trophic level makes a food chain less vulnerable to parasites

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Option 2__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Energy Flow in Food Chains:**

__
 
• **Loss of Energy at Each Trophic Level:**

 
 
• In a food chain, energy is **transferred from one trophic level to the next, typically starting from producers (plants)** to various levels of consumers.
 
• However, **during this transfer, a significant amount of energy is lost at each trophic level**, primarily as heat due to metabolic processes.
 
• ***Hence, option 2 is correct.***
 
 
 
• **10% Rule:**
 
 
• **According to the ecological 10% rule,** only about 10% of the energy at any given trophic level is passed on to the next level.
 
• **The remaining 90% is lost as heat,** used for metabolism, or left unutilized.
 
• This means that as energy moves up the food chain, there is progressively less energy available to support organisms at higher trophic levels.
 
 
 
• **Limitation on Trophic Levels:**
 
 
• Because of this progressive energy loss, food chains are generally limited to 4-5 trophic levels.
 
• Beyond this point, there is insufficient energy to support another level of consumers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Impact on Ecosystem Structure:**

 
 
• The limited number of trophic levels influences the structure and complexity of ecosystems.
 
• It affects the population sizes and the types of organisms that can be sustained at each level.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Efficiency:**
 
 
• The efficiency of energy transfer between trophic levels also determines the biomass and productivity of different ecosystems.

questions.question: Energy enters into the ecosystem through
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

__
 
• The producers are also called **autotrophs**.
 
• 'Auto' means self and 'trophs' means nutrient, *i.e.,* they can produce their own food.
 
• They produce food by capturing energy from nature which is solar energy, chemical energy, and geothermal energy.
 
• They use energy and inorganic nutrients to produce biomass, ATP and energy storage compounds (starch).

**Explanation**__

__
 
• The producers capture energy and nutrients from the environment.
 
• This **energy is then circulated** to other organisms **through the food chain**.
 
• The producers are consumed by herbivores that are in turn consumed by carnivores.
 
• No other organism except producers have the ability to capture energy from the environment.
 
• Hence, **energy enters the ecosystem through producers**.

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6dd88533bd479397c8ff098b2f7d94cd87266b920004f4f2f9d17ef4fb30dd9b.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Herbivores**

 
 
• Herbivores are that animals which feed on plants.
 
• They are also called the primary consumers because they are the first consumers after the producers.
 
• Example - deer, grasshopper, cow.
 
 
 
• **Carnivores**
 
 
• Carnivores are the animals that feed on other animals.
 
• They do not feed on plants and are hence called secondary or tertiary consumers depending upon their position in the food chain.
 
• Example - lion, snake, eagle.
 
 
 
• **Decomposers**
 
 
• All organisms are made of many complex organic biomolecules such as cellulose, chitin, liposaccharides, proteins, *etc.*
 
• Very few organisms in the nature have the ability to break down the complex biomolecules into simpler ones.
 
• This process of breakdown is called decomposition and the organisms capable of this are called decomposers.
 
• Example - most bacteria and a few fungi.

questions.question: The primary agent that helps in the decomposition of biodegradable matter in domestic sewage is __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**bacterium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bacteria** are the primary agents responsible for the decomposition of organic matter in domestic sewage.
 
• They break down complex organic compounds into simpler substances like carbon dioxide, water, and nutrients through biological processes.
 
• Decomposition by bacteria occurs under both aerobic (with oxygen) and anaerobic (without oxygen) conditions in sewage treatment plants.
 
• In the aerobic process, bacteria oxidize organic matter, while in the anaerobic process, they produce methane and other by-products.
 
• Bacteria play a crucial role in maintaining environmental balance by recycling nutrients and reducing organic pollution in wastewater.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Biodegradable Matter:** Organic substances that can be broken down by microorganisms into simpler, non-toxic forms.
 
• **Sewage Treatment:** A process that removes contaminants from wastewater, including physical, chemical, and biological treatments.
 
• **Aerobic Treatment:** A method where oxygen is supplied to bacteria to facilitate the breakdown of organic matter.
 
• **Anaerobic Treatment:** A process where bacteria decompose organic material in the absence of oxygen, often producing biogas.
 
• **Environmental Impact:** Effective sewage treatment reduces water pollution, prevents the spread of diseases, and promotes sustainable ecosystems.

questions.question: In a food chain of frog, grass, grasshopper, snake, what trophic level is assigned to frog?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3rd**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In a food chain, trophic levels represent the hierarchical positions that organisms occupy based on their source of energy.
 
• Grass is the primary producer and occupies the 1st trophic level.
 
• Grasshoppers feed on grass, making them primary consumers at the 2nd trophic level.
 
• Frogs feed on grasshoppers, thus they are secondary consumers occupying the 3rd trophic level.
 
• Snakes feed on frogs, making them tertiary consumers at the 4th trophic level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Trophic Levels**

 
 
• These are the positions that organisms occupy in a food chain, reflecting their feeding relationships and energy source.
 
• Primary producers (like plants) occupy the first trophic level, while various consumer levels follow.
 
 
 
• **Energy Flow**
 
 
• Energy flows through the food chain from producers to various levels of consumers.
 
• Only about 10% of energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next, with the rest lost as heat.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Pyramids**
 
 
• These are graphical representations showing the relationship between different trophic levels in an ecosystem.
 
• They can depict numbers, biomass, or energy at each level.

questions.question: What does a self-sustaining ecosystem mean?

options.text: The organic matter remains almost constant generation over generation.
It is not dependent on radiant energy for its maintenance.
No organisms are added or removed from the biotic component.
The organisms are well adapted to the local biotic components.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**No organisms are added or removed from the biotic component.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Self-sustaining ecosystem** refers to an ecosystem that can maintain its** balance and function **without external interference or inputs.
 
• It means that the ecosystem is able to** produce and recycle **all the necessary resources required for the** survival of its organisms.**
 
• A self-sustaining ecosystem means that no organisms are **added or removed **from the biotic component.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• An ecosystem needs **three primary elements** in order to be sustainable.

 
 
• **Energy availability: **In practically all societies,** light from the sun **serves as the primary energy source.
 
• **Nutritional availability: saprotrophic decomposers** guarantee that inorganic nutrients are continuously **recycled **in an ecosystem.
 
• **Recycling of wastes**: Some bacteria, such as denitrifying bacteria like **Nitrosomonas, **can detoxify toxic waste byproducts.

• Plants absorb **only 1-2% **of the **sunlight **that falls on leaves, as **98-99 % of the sunlight **is **reflected back** and converted to heat.
 
• Energy flow is **unidirectional** from the lower trophic level to the higher trophic level. 
 
• **10%** of energy is absorbed by each trophic level and the rest is lost in the environment.

questions.question: Which among the following is responsible for depletion of ozone layer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chlorine**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chlorine** is a major contributor to the depletion of the ozone layer.
 
• Chlorine atoms are released into the atmosphere from chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) and other ozone-depleting substances (ODS).
 
• Once in the stratosphere, chlorine atoms react with ozone (O₃) molecules, causing the ozone to break down into oxygen molecules (O₂).
 
• This breakdown reduces the concentration of ozone in the stratosphere, leading to the thinning of the ozone layer.
 
• The ozone layer is crucial for protecting life on Earth from harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the sun.
 
• International agreements like the Montreal Protocol have been established to phase out the production and use of CFCs and other ODS to protect the ozone layer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Montreal Protocol** was signed in 1987 and is considered one of the most successful environmental agreements to date.
 
• It aims to reduce and eventually eliminate the production and use of ODS.
 
• Since the implementation of the Montreal Protocol, the ozone layer has shown signs of recovery.
 
• Continued global cooperation and adherence to the protocol are essential for the full recovery of the ozone layer.

questions.question: The amount of energy that flows from one trophic level to another in a food chain is
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Only about 10% (or 0.1) of the energy from one trophic level is transferred to the next trophic level in a food chain.
 
• This is known as the "10% rule" in ecology.
 
• The remaining 90% of the energy is lost as heat, used for metabolic processes, or left in waste products.
 
• Energy transfer efficiency can vary between ecosystems and species but generally follows the 10% rule.
 
• Understanding energy flow is crucial for studying ecosystem dynamics and food web interactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Trophic Levels**

 
 
• These are the hierarchical levels in a food chain where organisms share the same function in the food web.
 
• Examples include primary producers, primary consumers, secondary consumers, and tertiary consumers.
 
 
 
• **Energy Pyramid**
 
 
• An energy pyramid visually represents the energy flow in an ecosystem.
 
• It shows the energy loss at each trophic level, with the largest energy quantities at the bottom (primary producers) and the smallest at the top (top predators).
 
 
 
• **Ecological Efficiency**
 
 
• This term refers to the efficiency with which energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next.
 
• It varies between different ecosystems and can be influenced by numerous factors such as species and environmental conditions.

questions.question: We come across various food chains in our ecosystem. How do you describe a food chain?

options.text: The process of converting sunlight into food energy
The transfer of energy from producers to consumers
The interconnection of various food webs in an ecosystem
The flow of nutrients from decomposers to producers

questions.solution:
```html

The correct answer is __**The transfer of energy from producers to consumers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A food chain represents the linear sequence of energy transfer from one organism to another within an ecosystem.
 
• Energy in a food chain flows from producers (organisms that synthesize their own food, like plants) to primary consumers (herbivores) and subsequently to secondary and tertiary consumers (carnivores and omnivores).
 
• The energy originates from sunlight, which is converted into chemical energy via photosynthesis by producers.
 
• Only about 10% of energy is transferred between trophic levels in a food chain, as per the "10% Energy Transfer Law." The rest is lost as heat or used for metabolic activities.
 
• Decomposers, like fungi and bacteria, play a crucial role at the end of the chain by breaking down dead organisms and recycling nutrients back into the ecosystem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Producer:** Organisms like green plants and algae that synthesize their own food using sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide through photosynthesis.
 
• **Primary Consumer:** Herbivores that feed directly on producers, such as deer, rabbits, and caterpillars.
 
• **Secondary Consumer:** Carnivores or omnivores that prey on herbivores, such as foxes, snakes, and birds.
 
• **Decomposer:** Organisms like fungi and bacteria that break down dead organisms and waste, recycling nutrients back into the ecosystem.
 
• **Food Web:** A complex network of interconnected food chains within an ecosystem, showcasing how energy flows through multiple pathways.

``

questions.question: Which biotic component of an ecosystem is present in the greatest number?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Producers**__.

**Note:** As per the official answer key, the correct answer is** Tertiary Consumers **but in actual the correct answer would be **Producers** because producers form the base of the ecological pyramid. As they are the primary source of energy for all other organisms in the ecosystem, producers are the most abundant biotic component.

**Source: ** https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/lebo114.pdf

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Producers** are the organisms in an ecosystem that produce energy-rich compounds like glucose through photosynthesis.
 
• They form the base of the food chain and are critical for energy flow in an ecosystem.
 
• Examples of producers include **plants, algae, and cyanobacteria**.
 
• Producers convert sunlight into chemical energy, which is utilized by all other biotic components.
 
• Their large numbers are essential for supporting the energy needs of the entire ecosystem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Primary Consumers**

 
 
• These organisms, also called herbivores, feed directly on producers.
 
• Examples include cows, deer, and caterpillars.
 
 
 
• **Secondary Consumers**
 
 
• These are carnivores or omnivores that feed on primary consumers.
 
• Examples include frogs, small birds, and some fish.
 
 
 
• **Tertiary Consumers**
 
 
• These are apex predators that consume secondary consumers.
 
• Examples include lions, eagles, and sharks.

questions.question: Which of the following is the chief role of Ozone Layer?

options.text: To decrease the volume of oxygen
To increase the volume of nitrogen

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To reduce Ultraviolet rays**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Ozone Layer is a part of the Earth's stratosphere that contains a high concentration of ozone (O₃) molecules.
 
• It plays a crucial role in absorbing the majority of the sun's harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation.
 
• By reducing the amount of UV radiation reaching the Earth's surface, the Ozone Layer helps to protect living organisms from DNA damage and skin cancers.
 
• The Ozone Layer also helps to regulate the temperature structure of the Earth's atmosphere, which is essential for weather and climate patterns.
 
• Depletion of the Ozone Layer can lead to increased UV radiation exposure, which can have adverse effects on human health, ecosystems, and wildlife.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ultraviolet (UV) Radiation**

 
 
• UV radiation is a form of electromagnetic radiation emitted by the sun and artificial sources like tanning beds.
 
• There are three types of UV radiation: UVA, UVB, and UVC, with UVC being the most harmful but mostly absorbed by the atmosphere.
 
 
 
• **Ozone Depletion**
 
 
• Ozone depletion refers to the thinning of the Earth's ozone layer caused primarily by human-made chemicals like chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs).
 
• Efforts like the Montreal Protocol have been implemented globally to reduce and eventually eliminate the production of ozone-depleting substances.
 
 
 
• **Greenhouse Effect**
 
 
• The greenhouse effect is a natural process that warms the Earth's surface, caused by greenhouse gases like carbon dioxide, methane, and water vapor trapping heat in the atmosphere.
 
• While the greenhouse effect is essential for life on Earth, human activities have enhanced this effect, leading to global warming and climate change.

questions.question: In a food chain, the base of energy pyramid consists of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**producers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In a food chain, **producers form the base** of the energy pyramid, as they are the primary source of energy for all other trophic levels.
 
• Producers are typically **autotrophic organisms**, such as plants, algae, and certain bacteria, that can synthesize their own food through photosynthesis or chemosynthesis.
 
• They convert solar energy into chemical energy stored in organic compounds, forming the foundation of the ecosystem's energy flow.
 
• The energy transfer between trophic levels is highly inefficient, with only about **10% of energy** being passed on to the next level, making producers critical for sustaining the ecosystem.
 
• Examples of producers include grass in a grassland ecosystem, phytoplankton in aquatic ecosystems, and trees in a forest ecosystem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Energy Pyramid:**

 
 
• An energy pyramid is a graphical representation of the energy flow within an ecosystem.
 
• It is divided into trophic levels, starting with producers at the base, followed by primary consumers, secondary consumers, and tertiary consumers.
 
• The width of each level represents the amount of energy available at that trophic level.
 
 
 
• **Trophic Levels:**
 
 
• Trophic levels refer to the hierarchical stages in a food chain, starting with producers (first level) and moving up to herbivores, carnivores, and apex predators.
 
• Energy transfer between these levels follows the 10% rule, where only 10% of energy from one level is passed to the next.
 
 
 
• **Photosynthesis:**
 
 
• Photosynthesis is the process by which producers convert solar energy, water, and carbon dioxide into glucose and oxygen.
 
• This chemical energy stored in glucose provides the foundation for the entire food chain.
 
 
 
• **Consumers:**
 
 
• Consumers depend on producers or other organisms for energy. They include primary consumers (herbivores), secondary consumers (carnivores), and tertiary consumers (top predators).
 
• Unlike producers, consumers cannot synthesize their own food and rely on external sources of energy.
 
 
 
• **Decomposers:**
 
 
• Decomposers, such as fungi and bacteria, break down organic matter from dead organisms, recycling nutrients back into the ecosystem.
 
• They play a critical role in maintaining the balance of the ecosystem by facilitating nutrient cycling.

questions.question: Which of the following options represents artificial ecosystems?

options.text: Zoo, national park, forest and pond ecosystem
Crop ecosystem, forest and grassland ecosystem
Fish farm, forest and ocean ecosystem
Fish farm, zoo, green house and hydroponics

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Fish farm, zoo, greenhouse, and hydroponics.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fish farms** are created by humans** to raise fish for food or other purposes**. They typically have a **controlled environment**, **with artificial water sources, feeding systems, and predator control.**
 
• **Zoos are created by humans** to house animals for public display. They typically have enclosures that are designed to mimic the animals' natural habitats, but they are still **artificial environments.**
 
• Greenhouses are **created by humans to control the environment for plant growth**. They typically have transparent walls and roofs that allow sunlight to enter, and they can be equipped with temperature and humidity control systems. 
 
• These are all examples of artificial ecosystems, which are ecosystems that have been created or modified by humans.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• National parks are areas of land that have been** designated by the government **to be protected from development. They typically **contain natural ecosystems**, such as** forests, grasslands, and wetlands. **
 
• Forests are ecosystems that are **dominated by trees**. They can be found in a variety of climates, and they provide a variety of benefits, such as clean air and water, wildlife habitat, and recreation opportunities. 
 
• Grasslands are ecosystems that are** dominated by grasses**. They can be found in a variety of climates, and they provide a variety of benefits, such as grazing for livestock, wildlife habitat, and carbon sequestration. 
 
• Ponds are freshwater ecosystems that are typically smaller than lakes. They can be found in a variety of habitats, and they provide a variety of benefits, such as fish habitat, water storage, and recreation opportunities.

questions.question: Which of the following items from daily household waste is non-biodegradable?

__

• **Non-biodegradable waste:** These are materials that do not decompose easily and remain in the environment for a long time, causing pollution. Examples include plastics, glass, and metals.

questions.question: What kind of radiation is absorbed by the ozone layer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ultraviolet radiation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The ozone layer is a region of Earth's stratosphere that absorbs most of the Sun's **ultraviolet (UV) radiation**.
 
• It contains a high concentration of ozone (O₃) molecules.
 
• The absorption of UV radiation by the ozone layer protects living organisms on Earth from potential damage such as skin cancer and cataracts.
 
• The ozone layer is mainly located in the lower portion of the stratosphere, from approximately 15 to 35 kilometers above Earth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ozone (O₃)**

 
 
• Ozone is a molecule composed of three oxygen atoms, formed naturally in the stratosphere.
 
• It is produced when oxygen molecules (O₂) are split by ultraviolet light and then recombine with other oxygen molecules.
 
• Ozone is crucial for absorbing the majority of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation.
 
• Though beneficial in the stratosphere, ozone can be a pollutant at ground level, contributing to smog.
 
 
 
• **Ultraviolet (UV) Radiation**
 
 
• Ultraviolet radiation is a type of electromagnetic radiation with wavelengths shorter than visible light but longer than X-rays.
 
• UV radiation is divided into three types based on wavelength: UVA, UVB, and UVC.
 
• UVC is the most harmful but is completely absorbed by the ozone layer and oxygen in the atmosphere.
 
• UVB is partially absorbed by the ozone layer and can cause skin burns and cancer.
 
• UVA has the least energy and is not absorbed by the ozone layer, but it can still cause skin aging and contribute to skin cancer.
 
 
 
• **Stratosphere**
 
 
• The stratosphere is the second major layer of Earth's atmosphere, just above the troposphere and below the mesosphere.
 
• It extends from about 10 to 50 kilometers above the Earth's surface.
 
• The stratosphere is characterized by a temperature inversion, meaning temperatures increase with altitude.
 
• This temperature increase is due to the absorption of ultraviolet radiation by the ozone layer.

questions.question: The arrows in a food chain represent:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Energy flow**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In a food chain, the arrows represent the **flow of energy** from one organism to another.
 
• Energy is transferred when one organism consumes another, starting from producers (plants) to primary consumers, secondary consumers, and so on.
 
• Producers, like plants, convert solar energy into chemical energy through photosynthesis, which is the base of energy flow in ecosystems.
 
• The energy flow follows the **10% rule**, where only about 10% of energy is transferred to the next trophic level, while the rest is lost as heat.
 
• This energy transfer is vital for sustaining life and maintaining ecological balance in ecosystems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Producers:** Organisms like plants and algae that produce their own food through photosynthesis and form the base of the food chain.
 
• **Consumers:** Organisms that depend on others for food, classified as primary (herbivores), secondary (carnivores), and tertiary consumers.
 
• **Decomposers:** Organisms like fungi and bacteria that break down dead matter and recycle nutrients back into the ecosystem.
 
• **Trophic Levels:** The hierarchical levels in a food chain, showing the position of organisms in the energy flow (e.g., producers, primary consumers, etc.).
 
• **10% Rule:** A principle of energy transfer stating that only 10% of energy is passed on to the next trophic level, with 90% lost as heat or used for metabolic processes.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are related to ecosystem?

(i) It consists of biotic components comprising living organisms.

(ii) All green plants and certain bacteria are producers.

(iii) Decomposers break-down complex organic into simple organic substance.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3) Only (i) and (ii)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An ecosystem comprises both biotic (living organisms) and abiotic (non-living elements) components.
 
• Green plants and certain bacteria are producers because they can manufacture their own food through photosynthesis or chemosynthesis.
 
• Decomposers, such as fungi and bacteria, break down dead organic matter into simpler inorganic substances, recycling nutrients back into the ecosystem.
 
• Statements (i) and (ii) are correct. Statement (iii) is incorrect because decomposers break down complex organic substances into simple inorganic substances, not organic.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ecosystem:**

 
 
• An ecosystem is a community of living organisms (plants, animals, and microbes) interacting with their physical environment (air, water, soil).
 
• It involves both biotic and abiotic components that interact as a system.
 
• Energy flows through an ecosystem in one direction—usually from the sun, through photosynthetic organisms (producers), to herbivores (consumers), and finally to decomposers.
 
 
 
• **Producers:**
 
 
• Producers, or autotrophs, are organisms that produce their own food through photosynthesis (using sunlight) or chemosynthesis (using chemical energy).
 
• Examples include green plants, algae, and certain bacteria.
 
 
 
• **Consumers:**
 
 
• Consumers, or heterotrophs, are organisms that cannot produce their own food and depend on other organisms for nutrition.
 
• They are categorized into primary consumers (herbivores), secondary consumers (carnivores that eat herbivores), and tertiary consumers (carnivores that eat other carnivores).
 
 
 
• **Decomposers:**
 
 
• Decomposers are organisms that break down dead or decaying organisms, and in doing so, carry out the natural process of decomposition.
 
• They play a critical role in nutrient cycling by converting organic materials back into inorganic substances, which can be used by producers.
 
• Examples include fungi, bacteria, and certain insects.

questions.question: Which of the following have the largest population in a food chain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __** Decomposers**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Decomposers are an integral part of food chain and it is the largest population in food chain.

__
 
• Decomposers receive nutrients and energy by breaking down dead animals and animal waste.
 
• Via this process, decomposers return nutrients, such as carbon and nitrogen, to the ecosystem.
 
• These nutrients are transferred back to the environment so that they can be utilized by the producers.
 
• These are passed on to other species as they are ingested or consumed. Many of these nutrients are released back into the soil so that the seeds of the plants can be taken up.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Food chain**:​ The sequence of living organisms in a community in which one organism consumes another organism to transfer food energy is called a food chain.
 
• In simple words, A list of organisms showing **'who eats** **whom' **is called the food chain.
 
• The food can be transferred from one organism to the other through the food chain.
 
• Each step in the food chain is represented by a trophic level.
 
• Producers occupy the base of the food chain, producers are followed by **Primary Consumers → Secondary consumers → Tertiary consumers → Decomposers.**
 
• **Herbivores** are the animals that eat plants for their nutrition.
 
• They occupy the position of primary consumers. Example - **Cow, goat, deer, grasshopper, etc.**
 
• Example of a food chain - **Grass → grasshopper → frog → snake**
 
• Here, Grass represents the Producer, grasshopper the primary consumer, frog the secondary consumer & snake is the tertiary consumer.

questions.question:
Which of the following is/are correct regarding the components of an ecosystem?

A. Living organisms - Abiotic Component

B. Soil - Biotic component

C. Minerals - Abiotic component
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only C**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** **Ecosystem Components:**

 
• An ecosystem consists of two main components: biotic (living) and abiotic (non-living).
 
• Biotic components include all living organisms, such as plants, animals, fungi, and bacteria.
 
• Abiotic components include non-living factors, such as soil, water, air, minerals, and sunlight.
 
• These components interact with each other, creating a complex and dynamic system.
 
• The flow of energy and the cycling of nutrients are essential processes in an ecosystem.
 
• Biotic factors are influenced by abiotic factors, and vice versa.
 
• For example, plants (biotic) rely on sunlight, water, and minerals (abiotic) for growth.
 
• Animals (biotic) depend on plants (biotic) and water (abiotic) for survival.
 
• Soil (abiotic) is a crucial component that supports plant growth and provides habitat for various organisms (biotic).
 
• Soil contains many minerals.
 
• Minerals are inorganic substances that are essential for the growth and development of living organisms.
 
• Minerals in the soil are absorbed by plants and then passed on to animals through the food chain.
 
• The availability of minerals can significantly affect the health and productivity of an ecosystem.
 
• Water (abiotic) is essential for all living organisms and plays a vital role in nutrient transport and other biological processes.
 
• Air (abiotic) provides oxygen for respiration and carbon dioxide for photosynthesis.
 
• Sunlight (abiotic) is the primary source of energy for most ecosystems.
 
• The interactions between biotic and abiotic components determine the structure and function of an ecosystem.
 
• Ecosystems are constantly changing due to natural and human-induced factors.
 
• The balance between biotic and abiotic factors is crucial for maintaining ecosystem stability.
 
• Therefore, minerals are correctly classified as an abiotic component of an ecosystem.
 
• Living organisms are correctly classified as a biotic component.
 
• Soil is correctly classified as an abiotic component, although it contains biotic organisms.

questions.question: The pyramid that cannot be inverted in a stable ecosystem, is pyramid of
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

__
 
• **Ecological pyramids** are graphical representations of trophic systems in an ecosystem.
 
• **Shape of pyramid** can be **upright** (base broader than top), **inverted** (top broader than base) or variable.
 
• They are mainly of 3 types:

 
• **Pyramid of Number** -

 
 
• It is based on the number of individuals in each trophic level.
 
 
 
• **Pyramid of Biomass** - 
 
 
• It is based on the quantitative biomass of organisms present in unit area (standing crop), for each trophic level.
 
 
 
• **Pyramid of Energy** -
 
 
• It is based on the **energy content available** at each trophic level.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Trophic system** refers to the system in which **energy flows from one trophic level to another**.
 
• **Trophic level** is the specific place in the food chain that is occupied by an organism based on their source of food.
 
• In an ecosystem, we find **unidirectional flow of energy** from Sun to producers to consumers.
 
• Ecosystems need a **constant supply of energy** to synthesize the molecules required in order to **counteract the universal tendency of increasing disorderliness**.
 
• In a grazing food chain, the energy trapped by the producer is passed on to the consumer or leads to death, which starts the detritus food chain and the energy is passed on to the decomposer.
 
• According to **Lindeman's 10% Law**, only **10% of the energy in a trophic level is transferred to the next**, so that there can only be a **limited number of trophic levels** in each ecological pyramid.

**Explanation:**__

__
 
• The **pyramid of energy** is **always upright** because of the 10% Law, meaning **energy keeps decreasing at successive trophic levels**.
 
• The **unidirectional flow of energy gives stability** to the ecosystem.
 
• Therefore, **the pyramid of energy can never be inverted in a stable ecosystem**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6dd88533bd479397c8ff098b2f7d94cd87266b920004f4f2f9d17ef4fb30dd9b.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **pyramid of number** is upright in grassland ecosystem, while **inverted in parasitic ecosystem** and variable in forest ecosystem.
 
• The **pyramid of biomass** is usually upright, but can be **inverted in pond ecosystem**.

questions.question: __________ can be visualized as a functional unit of nature, where living organisms interact among themselves and also with the surrounding physical environment.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**An ecosystem**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• ​Here is a brief explanation about an ecosystem:
 
• **Interaction of Life and Non-Life:**
 
 
• **​**An ecosystem is a community of **living organisms (plants, animals, microbes) interacting amongst themselves and with their non-living surroundings (atmosphere, earth, sun, soil, climate).**
 
 
 
• **Energy Flow:**
 
 
• **​**The ecosystem is characterized by the flow of energy and matter through food chains and food webs.
 
• It starts with the energy from the sun being captured by plants in the process of photosynthesis.
 
 
 
• **Nutrient Cycling:**
 
 
• **​**In an ecosystem, nutrients are cycled through various living and non-living components.
 
• This involves processes like decomposition and nutrient absorption by plants.
 
 
 
• **Different Types:**
 
 
• **​**Ecosystems can vary widely in size and characteristics, from a small pond to a large forest or even an entire biome such as a desert or tundra.
 
 
 
• **Balance:**
 
 
• **​**Ecosystems inherently maintain a balance between different species and resources.
 
• However, human intervention or natural disasters can disrupt this balance, affecting the entire ecosystem's functionality.

questions.question: Select the correct statement.

options.text: An open ecosystem exchanges both energy and matter with its surroundings.
A closed ecosystem exchanges both energy and matter with its surroundings.
A closed ecosystem exchanges only matter and no energy with its surroundings.
An open ecosystem exchanges only energy and no matter with its surroundings.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**An open ecosystem exchanges both energy and matter with its surroundings.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An ecosystem is a complex network of living organisms, their physical environment, and the interactions between them.
 
• The ecosystem can either be an open system or a closed system.
 
• .An open system is a system that can exchange both matter and energy with its surroundings.
 
• In an open ecosystem, there is a continuous exchange of matter and energy between the biotic and abiotic components of the ecosystem and the surrounding environment.
 
• This exchange of matter and energy is crucial for the survival of the organisms in the ecosystem.
 
• Examples of open ecosystems include forests, grasslands, and oceans.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Closed Ecosystem:**

 
 
• ​A closed system is a system that can exchange energy but not matter with its surroundings.
 
• In a closed ecosystem, there is no exchange of matter with the surrounding environment.
 
• The matter within the ecosystem is recycled and reused, and there are no inputs or outputs of matter.
 
• Energy, on the other hand, can enter and leave the ecosystem.
 
• An example of a closed ecosystem is a terrarium or an aquarium.
